bilingual.notes: Bilingual, PreK-12 endorsement under R7-2-615(J). Full endorsement = (a) approved bilingual program OR 21 semester hours of specified coursework, (b) 3-hr practicum OR 2 years bilingual classroom experience, (c) verified proficiency in a world language other than English (seven options: Arizona Classroom Spanish Proficiency Exam, AEPA/NES foreign-language portion, tribal verification of an American Indian language, comparable out-of-state exam, world-language degree, 3 years foreign-language teaching, or ACTFL OPI). Provisional endorsement (3 years, non-renewable) = prerequisite certificate + language-proficiency verification only.

eld.notes: English as a Second Language (ESL), PreK-12 endorsement under R7-2-615(K). Full endorsement = (a) approved ESL program OR 18 semester hours of specified coursework, (b) 3-hr ESL practicum OR 2 years ESL/bilingual experience, (c) a 'second language learning experience' (six-hour single-language coursework, intensive language training, third-semester placement, ACTFL OPI intermediate-low, AZ Spanish Proficiency Exam, American Indian language verification, or AEPA/NES foreign-language exam). The second-language requirement is exposure-not verified proficiency, hence languageProficiency=false. Provisional ESL = 6 hours of ESL coursework including methods (3 yrs, non-renewable). ADE explicitly states the ESL endorsement also authorizes teaching in a Structured English Immersion setting.

sei.notes: Universal mandate: per R7-2-615(L) and ADE OELAS, 'a Provisional or full SEI endorsement, or an ESL or Bilingual endorsement, shall be required of a teacher who is instructing students in a sheltered English immersion or structured English immersion model.' Originating in Proposition 203 (2000) and HB 2064 (2006), Arizona has the country's broadest teacher-of-EL credentialing mandate. The full SEI endorsement is earnable via 3 semester hours of approved coursework or 45 clock hours of approved professional development under A.R.S. § 15-756.09(B); the provisional version is 1 semester hour or 15 clock hours (3 years, non-renewable). Spring 2019 legislation reduced the daily SEI ELD block from 4 hours to 2 hours and re-opened broader access to dual-language and bilingual program models, but did not repeal the teacher endorsement mandate.

history.title: Flores v. Arizona filed (D. Ariz. CV-92-596-TUC-RCC)
history.description: Plaintiff parents in the Nogales Unified School District filed a class action alleging Arizona was violating the Equal Educational Opportunities Act of 1974 by underfunding programs for EL students. The case (later named Flores v. Arizona) drove the next two decades of EL policy in the state, leading to the 2000 district-court ruling that Arizona's per-pupil EL funding was "arbitrary and capricious" and forcing the legislature to act on EL teacher preparation and program funding. The case ultimately produced Horne v. Flores at the U.S. Supreme Court in 2009.

history.title: Voters approve Proposition 203 (English for the Children)
history.description: Proposition 203 amends Arizona law to require Structured English Immersion as the default instructional model for ELs and lays the foundation for the universal SEI-endorsement mandate later codified in R7-2-615(L) and A.R.S. § 15-756.09.

history.title: HB 2064 establishes SEI endorsement infrastructure
history.description: HB 2064 (50th Legislature, 2nd Regular Session) creates the Arizona English Language Learners Task Force and authorizes the SEI endorsement and SEI model — setting the 4-hour daily ELD block standard and embedding the SEI endorsement requirement for any teacher instructing ELs in an SEI setting.

history.title: Horne v. Flores decided by U.S. Supreme Court (557 U.S. 433)
history.description: In a 5–4 decision, the U.S. Supreme Court vacated the lower courts' rulings against Arizona in the long-running Flores v. Arizona litigation and remanded for reconsideration in light of changed circumstances — namely Proposition 203's SEI mandate, HB 2064's new EL Task Force and SEI endorsement, and the federal No Child Left Behind framework. The decision narrowed the EEOA enforcement leverage federal courts had previously exercised over state EL programs and is the controlling SCOTUS precedent on EEOA "appropriate action" claims. The companion HB 2064 SEI infrastructure remained in force.

history.title: Arizona Seal of Biliteracy authorized (SB 1239)
history.description: Governor signed SB 1239 (A.R.S. § 15-258) creating the Arizona State Seal of Biliteracy, recognizing high school graduates who attain proficiency in English and one or more world languages.

history.title: HB 2435 reduces daily SEI/ELD block from 4 hours to 2
history.description: Spring 2019 legislation (HB 2435, signed July 2019) reduced the mandatory daily SEI English Language Development block from 4 hours to 2 hours and re-opened access to dual-language and bilingual program models. The teacher-of-EL endorsement mandate under R7-2-615(L) was not repealed.
